claims.text: Dual-phase lamellar colonies in eutectic high-entropy alloys contain numerous internal boundaries that act as microcrack-initiation sites during room-temperature tensile loading.
Melt spinning at a cooling rate greater than 10^5 K/s will refine the lamellar spacing in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Annealing at 700°C for 5 minutes after melt spinning will relieve residual stresses.
Annealing at 700°C for 5 minutes will avoid significant coarsening of the refined lamellar structure.
The combined rapid-solidification and annealing treatment will enhance the integrity of internal boundaries.
Finer lamellar spacing minimizes the size of potential microcrack-initiation sites.
Refinement of the lamellar structure produces grain-boundary strengthening that increases tensile strength.
A refined lamellar structure reduces effective crack-propagation paths.
Reducing effective crack-propagation paths improves room-temperature tensile ductility.
The treatment will mitigate microcrack initiation relative to conventional processing.
The treatment will increase yield strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The treatment will increase ultimate tensile strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The treatment will increase elongation at failure relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Conventional processing produces coarse lamellar colonies that are prone to microcracking.
The treatment will only remain effective if the anneal does not cause deleterious phase transformations or coarsening.
The effectiveness of the treatment may vary among alloy compositions with different sensitivities to annealing.
